findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. The refusal always tells the user to add a trusted main-checkout entry. But when that entry is already trusted and the worktree has an untrusted entry, `_codex_trust` refuses because it requires every matching entry to be trusted. Adding the named entry cannot resolve the refusal. The new test explicitly creates this state at `tests/test_codex_trust_parent.py:50`; the refusal needs to identify the entry that must change.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The new parent-only case runs `forge doctor` and checks its message, but never runs a Codex turn. The existing `forge work` refusal test uses an explicitly untrusted project entry instead. The suite can therefore pass if doctor rejects a trusted parent while the worker still starts a turn for that same configuration, leaving the Done-when refusal unproved at the worker's entry point.
